key_idea: The smallest square enclosing a circle has side 2r, and the axis-aligned one centred at (x,y) already has integer corners.
sketch: Print (x-r,y-r), (x+r,y-r), (x+r,y+r), (x-r,y+r) in order. Use 64-bit integers since coordinates reach 2e9. Any orientation is accepted, so the sample checker shows a mismatch against the rotated sample squares; samples_passed is based on my own validator, which checked on the samples and 200 random cases that the four points form a square of side exactly 2r centred on the circle centre.
